prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour Party Manifesto 2019 – Summary (under 500 words)

Vision and funding
- “Real change” to shift wealth and power from a privileged few, end austerity and tackle the climate emergency.
- Fair tax plan: raise income tax on earnings above £80,000; reverse parts of corporation tax cuts; no VAT rise; major anti-avoidance drive; 20:1 public-sector pay ratio cap; restore public sector pay with above-inflation rises.
- Investment: £400bn National Transformation Fund (incl. £250bn Green Transformation Fund); National Investment Bank and Regional Development Banks; £150bn Social Transformation Fund for schools, hospitals, housing and care.

Green Industrial Revolution
- Target majority of UK emissions cuts by 2030; 90% of electricity and 50% of heat from low-carbon by 2030.
- 1 million climate jobs; ban fracking; windfall tax on oil firms; mass home retrofits and zero‑carbon standard for new homes; large-scale wind/solar, trial tidal and hydrogen; grid upgrades and storage.
- Public ownership of energy and water; community energy expansion.
- Transport: bring rail into public ownership; electrification, HS2 to Scotland and “Crossrail for the North”; regulate/municipalise buses (free for under‑25s where councils run routes); boost walking/cycling; end new petrol/diesel car sales by 2030; expand EV charging.

Economy, work and rights
- Real Living Wage £10+ for all 16+; ban zero-hours; day‑one rights; single “worker” status; sectoral collective bargaining.
- Reduce average full-time week to 32 hours within a decade with no loss of pay; strengthen unions; inclusive ownership funds (up to 10% employee stakes).
- Tough late-payment rules; tailored support for self‑employed.

Public services, NHS and care
- End outsourcing and PFI; presumption to insource.
- NHS: average 4.3% annual funding rise; end privatisation; free prescriptions; restore public health; invest in staff, scanners, IT and mental health (parity with physical health).
- Social care: National Care Service with free personal care, better conditions for care workers, more packages to support independent living.

Education and skills
- National Education Service: restore Sure Start (Sure Start Plus), 30 hours free pre‑school for 2–4‑year‑olds, extend paid maternity leave to 12 months.
- Schools: fair funding, max primary classes of 30, scrap SATs, Arts Premium, bring academies/free schools under democratic local control, free school meals for all primaries.
- Further/higher: lifelong learning entitlements; abolish tuition fees; restore maintenance grants; boost ESOL and adult learning.

Housing
- Build 1m+ council and social homes over a decade (150k/yr; 100k council); redefine “affordable” by income; end Right to Buy; “use it or lose it” on stalled sites.
- Private renting: rent controls, open‑ended tenancies, minimum standards/licensing, end no‑fault evictions; leasehold reform; £1bn fire safety fund; end rough sleeping in five years.

Justice, security and communities
- Rebuild neighbourhood policing; public health approach to crime; restore legal aid; reunify probation publicly; presumption against short sentences.
- Free full‑fibre broadband for all by 2030 via public ownership; Digital Rights and duty of care online.
- Strengthen local government, high streets (Post Bank, stop Crown Post Office closures), co-operatives and community wealth building.

Equality, migration and social security
- Department for Women and Equalities; close gender pay gap by 2030; stronger disability, race and LGBT+ rights.
- End the “hostile environment”; scrap 2014 Immigration Act; end indefinite detention; close Yarl’s Wood/Brook House; automatic right to remain for EU citizens.
- Scrap Universal Credit; immediate mitigations (end five‑week wait, end sanctions, scrap cap and two‑child limit); raise ESA; increase Carer’s Allowance; improve disability assessments.

Brexit and constitution
- Final‑say referendum within six months: credible leave deal (customs union, close single market alignment, rights and standards) vs remain; implement result.
- Abolish House of Lords for an elected Senate after a Constitutional Convention; votes at 16; automatic voter registration; curb dark money and lobbying.

Foreign policy and defence
- Human rights–led diplomacy; War Powers Act; recognise Palestine; suspend arms sales linked to abuses; rebuild climate diplomacy.
- Maintain NATO and 2% defence spending; renew Trident; improve forces’ pay, housing and veteran support.
